name: scalar-writers
what: time of one call of the escape of one context (xml, json, js, css, troff) for one value, in a loop over a list of 64 values that moves the output position by the count, as a render does; ns per value
purpose_in_the_task_list: Owner, 2026-11-14: the word tables of 256 entries for each context take about 10 KiB. Hypothesis: a table of 128 words for the bytes under 0x80, with a byte from 0x80 on written as the byte itself (no context escapes such a byte, checked in include/mustache/escape.hpp of 843ca17), keeps the time of the word tables. This run answers whether it does
method: not the method of mbedded-cbor/bench/README.md: one run, 6 rounds, the arm order alternates by round (forward, then reversed), each process 5 repetitions of 2^22 input bytes for each input, timed with std::chrono::steady_clock; arm 6 is arm 2 built twice; arms 0 and 1 are not in this run; sysbench cpu 10 times for 1 s before the first round; each arm is held to the bytes of the arm before (the writers of 4dac08e, compiled in the same binary) before it is timed (every byte value alone and beside a letter, 16 pieces of js and troff at every position of every length 0 to 20, and every value of the inputs), with a room of escaped_size_max_in(context, n) + 32 bytes and guard bytes behind it; no gate, no steal

arms.2: each piece of output, a plain byte too, is one 8-byte word stored through std::span<char, 8>, std::bit_cast and std::copy_n, and the count moves on by the length of the piece; the word of each byte comes from a table of 256 words for each context, built at compile time; js tests the first byte of U+2028 and U+2029 and then starts_with; troff writes the first and the last place of a line apart from the table
arms.6: the same code as arm 2, a second binary: the noise of the cell
arms.7: arm 2 with a table of 128 words for each context, for the bytes under 0x80; a byte from 0x80 on is written as the byte itself (a compare and a branch or a select for each input byte); a static_assert in probe.cpp checks that each word function of the five contexts gives the byte itself for every byte from 0x80 on

inputs.<n>-<p>: 64 values of n bytes (16, 64, 1024) from letters, digits and a space; each byte is a mark of the context with the probability p percent (0 or 5); marks: xml &<>"', json " \ line feed and 0x01, js ' < \ /, css ' } < \, troff \ " ' ` ~ ^; fixed seed
inputs.lines-<n>-<p>: troff only: the same with a line feed at every 16th byte

builds: g++-16 and clang++-23, -O2 and -Os, -march=x86-64-v3; -std=c++26 -DNDEBUG -Wall -Wextra -Werror -falign-functions=64 -falign-loops=64 (g++ also -falign-jumps=64) -DARM=<arm>; one binary for each arm and build
arms_in_this_run: 2 6 7 (order of the first round; the order reverses in each even round)
headers: none (probe.cpp holds a copy of the writers of 4dac08e and the forms of arms 2 to 7)
